summary: On Friday, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro announced that authorities arrested Melissa L. Farris for vandalizing the National World War II Memorial, which honors more than 400,000 Americans killed in World War II.
The vandalism occurred Thursday at the National Mall, where graffiti reading "Clean hands, dirty money" was spray-painted on the monument and soap clogged a fountain, forcing the memorial to close.

Pirro's office filed two felony charges against Farris: Depredation Against Property of the United States and Destruction of Veterans' Memorials, offenses carrying penalties of up to 10 years in prison.
The U.S. Department of the Interior called the act "an utter disgrace," while the Veterans of Foreign Wars described it as "a slap in the face" to veterans and their families.

summary: On Friday, President Donald Trump filed an emergency request with the Supreme Court to resume his $400 million White House ballroom project after lower courts halted above-ground construction.

Architect Shalom Baranes designed the ballroom at approximately 89,000 square feet, nearly double the Executive Mansion's 55,000 square feet. Trump aims to complete it by summer 2028.

Solicitor General John Sauer argued the construction is 'absolutely required' for presidential safety, calling the injunction 'judicial overreach.' The court paused its ruling for 14 days to allow the appeal.

The National Trust for Historic Preservation brought the case last year, arguing Congress never authorized the Executive Branch to reshape the White House. This marks the first Supreme Court challenge to Trump's projects.

District Judge Christopher Cooper will review these moves after previously blocking a closure he deemed "ill-informed and seemingly preordained." Democratic Rep. Joyce Beatty denounced the plan as circumventing court rulings.
The inscription serves as a workaround to federal law banning new memorials at the site. Trump's name was removed in June after a court order, though tarps still cover the facade.
Kennedy Center officials must submit the renovation plan to Judge Cooper next week. These moves align with Trump's broader capital remodeling, including work at the East Wing and East Potomac Park.

summary: On Friday, Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty in Manhattan federal court to two stalking charges resulting in the death of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, with Judge Margaret Garnett scheduling sentencing for December 18, 2026.

Mangione detailed his intent to kill an insurance executive after years of enduring severe back pain and frustration navigating the health system, confessing he used a 3D-printed pistol to ambush Thompson outside a Midtown Manhattan hotel.

Defense attorney Karen Friedman Agnifilo announced plans to seek dismissal of state murder charges on double jeopardy grounds, while Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg's office maintains the state case involves distinct legal harms and intends to proceed with trial.

Thompson's family expressed gratitude that the federal justice system held the perpetrator accountable, stating in a statement the plea marks "an important step toward justice for Brian and for our family."

As legal battles over double jeopardy protections intensify, the court must determine whether the federal guilty plea bars the state from pursuing further prosecution ahead of the scheduled September 8 trial and December 18 sentencing.

As national security adviser to Vice President Vance, Baker helped craft Vance's speech to the Munich Security Conference last year, where the vice president warned European leaders about democratic backsliding and external threats from China and Russia.

Previously a foreign service officer at the State Department several years ago, Baker stayed on months longer than planned to assist with transitions; Cliff Sims and Mike Needham now hold the national security roles Baker vacated.
Vance described Baker as "exceptionally gifted" and "indispensable," while Secretary Rubio called him "an invaluable asset." Baker called his tenure "an amazing journey" in a statement to Axios.

Baker's departure marks the latest change to a national security team undergoing a shake-up in recent months, alongside announced departures of press secretary Karoline Leavitt and counsel David Warrington.

summary: On Wednesday, the FDA upgraded the recall of nearly 1.6 million cartons of eggs to "Class I," its highest risk level, warning consumers that exposure could cause serious adverse health consequences or death.

Midwest Poultry Services, based in North Manchester, Indiana, initiated the recall in July after determining that 1,589,577 cartons of eggs produced in Texas between June 6 and July 3 "have the potential to be contaminated."

Since late July, the CDC has documented a Salmonella Enteritidis outbreak resulting in 345 reported infections and 36 hospitalizations across 27 states, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Recalled eggs were distributed to Kroger and Brookshire Grocery stores across Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Texas. Midwest Poultry Services urged consumers to return products for a refund.

The FDA explained the classification should not be viewed "as an expansion or change" to the initial recall, while symptoms of Salmonella Enteritidis include fever, vomiting, and diarrhea beginning six hours to six days after exposure.
title: FDA Upgrades Egg Recall Linked to Salmonella to Highest Health Risk Level

Rising exploitation reports prompted the probe, with Roblox reporting 65,381 instances of suspected child sexual exploitation to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children in 2025, more than double the 2024 total.
Hawley argued the platform markets itself as a safe playground for children as young as 5, yet Roblox averages more than 80 million daily players, roughly 40 percent of whom are under 13.

In response, Roblox Chief Safety Officer Matt Kaufman stated the company is built on "the foundation of safety" and does not compromise on that commitment, adding they look forward to sharing protective measures.
The inquiry follows child-safety lawsuits from multiple states, including Ohio and Florida, with Roblox required to produce documents and answer questions by August 31, 2026.
title: Senate panel investigates kids safety issues in online game Roblox

summary: On Friday, the Maryland Tax Court struck down the state's digital advertising tax, ordering refunds to Apple, Google, and Peacock TV for taxes collected under the unconstitutional law.

Enacted in 2021 to fund the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, the Digital Advertising Gross Revenues Tax targeted companies with at least $100 million in global revenue at graduated rates from 2.5% to 10%.
The court found the tax violates the 1998 Internet Tax Freedom Act by discriminating against digital advertising while not taxing similar print, billboard, or television ads equally.
Comptroller Brooke Lierman and legislative leaders said they "respectfully disagree" with the ruling and will pursue judicial review by the circuit court within 30 days.
Policymakers in Illinois and Utah, which adopted similar taxes this year, are monitoring the decision closely as legal experts expect other states will face identical constitutional challenges.
title: Maryland Tax Court Voids Digital Ad Tax, Orders Refunds to Apple, Google and Peacock TV

Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem announced plans to end Somali TPS citing improved conditions; plaintiffs argued the administration acted with bias, citing Trump's descriptions of Somalis as "garbage" and "low IQ people."

The Supreme Court curtailed judicial review of TPS terminations for 13 countries, significantly strengthening the administration's legal position regarding the effort to end protections for Somali beneficiaries.

Roughly 1,100 Somalis now face potential deportation and loss of work authorization; Representative Andy Ogles praised the ruling on Aug 14, claiming "maximum pressure works" regarding his impeachment efforts.
This decision advances the administration's broader push to terminate TPS designations for nations including Haiti, Syria, and Ethiopia, though only protections for Ethiopia remain blocked by judges.
title: US judge clears way for Trump to end Somalis' deportation protections

Judge Richard Leon ruled that the tribe had not shown the project would alter its reservation boundaries without congressional authorization or amount to unlawful trespassing.

The Tohono O’odham Nation argued that construction could damage sacred mountains and natural resources, disrupt religious practices, and separate families and communities that live on both sides of the U.S.-Mexico border.

Leon concluded that, at this stage, the federal government’s interests in border security, immigration enforcement and public safety outweighed the potential harms cited by the tribe, allowing the project to proceed.
title: Judge refuses to block Trump administration from building border wall along tribe's reservation

Historians and educators who reviewed the material criticized it for presenting Western civilization and Christianity as closely intertwined while portraying Islam in an overly negative and historically selective way.

Aycock wrote that the plaintiffs provided "minimal evidence" to prove an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, concluding they "wholly failed to carry their burden" to justify court intervention at this preliminary stage.

summary: On Monday, the Michigan Public Service Commission urged lawmakers to end yearly utility rate hikes, with Chair Dan Scripps detailing the recommendations in a letter to Governor Gretchen Whitmer proposing how DTE Electric and Consumers Energy earn profits.

State law currently allows utilities to file for rate hikes every 12 months, incentivizing expensive capital projects over maintenance. Regulators argue this regulatory model unnecessarily drives up household costs for DTE and Consumers customers.

Michigan households recently absorbed major rate hikes: $242.4 million for DTE in February and $276.6 million for Consumers in March. DTE then requested $474 million more in April, while Consumers sought $456 million in June.

The MPSC recommends requiring competitive bidding for infrastructure and authorizing virtual power plants to improve efficiency. Regulators also propose locking data center rules into statute to ensure facilities pay for high-voltage lines rather than shifting costs.

Regulators seek to align low-income assistance with the Michigan Energy Assistance Program threshold of 60% of state median income. This follows a June 11 order aiming to keep household energy costs under 6% of income.
title: Michigan regulators ask lawmakers to end annual rate hikes, change how DTE, Consumers make money

Fry noted the 62-year-old candidate understands the struggles families face from her hardscrabble upbringing. "President Trump needs fighters and allies in the Senate who will show up every day and get results," Fry said.

Tensions surfaced between Fry and the committee supporting Graham, which noted Trump initially called Fry "outstanding" before backing Graham instead. Fry, who finished third in the primary, now joins other powerful Republicans supporting her.
title: Russell Fry endorses Darline Graham in South Carolina primary runoff

Prosecutors allege Thao became "angry" and concerned about her political future, pressuring California Waste Solutions owners to pay a reporter's associate $10,000 to prevent publication of a story.
Investigators also allege one of the business owners kept dozens of secret recordings, photos, and videos of politicians in "compromising positions," potentially complicating Thao's legal situation.

Conservative commentator Benny Johnson and the account Libs of TikTok shared compilations of her past posts, with one clip of her remarks having been viewed over 300,000 times.
A recent Fox News poll showed Republican Mike Rogers leading El-Sayed 51 percent to 47 percent, though it remains unclear what bearing Abdelhadi's comments will have on the Senate bid.

Last month, President Trump announced a breakthrough in his Gaza plan, involving an International Stabilization Force and a new Palestinian police force, which Israel and Hamas ostensibly accepted to end the two-year war.

The Hamas-led interior ministry confirmed the "assassination" of police colonel Jamal Abu Kmail, while the Israeli military stated the Khan Younis strike targeted a Hamas commander planning an attack on its troops.

title: IDF Kills Hamas Commander Who Invaded Israel on October 7 in Targeted Gaza Strike

summary: The Democratic National Committee is scheduled to approve a new 2028 presidential primary calendar Saturday in Austin, Texas , making South Carolina first on Jan. 22, followed by Nevada on Feb. 1.

Shifting from Iowa and New Hampshire's traditional dominance, DNC Chairman Ken Martin championed the plan as the "most diverse calendar in our party's history." The change prioritizes states reflecting the nation's demographic diversity.

Five of the six early states are competitive general election battlegrounds, positioning candidates to secure 43 Electoral College votes before Super Tuesday—a significant portion of the 270 needed to win.

Campaigns will prioritize Black and Latino voters alongside organized labor in Nevada, Michigan, and Virginia, which represent distinct union constituencies from service industries to manufacturing and federal employment.

Party strategist Karen Finney stated the structure compels candidates to demonstrate nationwide appeal, declaring, "If you can't go to every part of this country and make your case, you should not be running for president.
title: Democrats' Early 2028 Primary Calendar Set to Prioritize Black and Latino Voters, Organized Labor

Abbott claimed the facilities 'appear designed to single out one subset of the population for special treatment based on religion.' He urged Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to launch federal investigations, alleging constitutional violations.

State Sen. Tan Parker sent inquiries Thursday regarding the project's private funding. Abbott previously threatened $530,000 in grants for Grand Prairie over a 'Muslims only' water park event, establishing a pattern of funding-based pressure.

summary: Department of Homeland Security agents conducted a widespread undercover surveillance operation in Minnesota, targeting progressive activist groups and major labor unions protesting a massive federal immigration crackdown in the Minneapolis area.

The programs, dubbed "Operation Puppet Master" and "Project Whipple Shield," were aimed at investigating what federal officials characterized as a network aiding "violent opportunists and agitators," following the deployment of 3,000 DHS officers to the region.

Undercover officers secretly infiltrated public activist meetings at churches, libraries, schools, and parks—monitoring encrypted chat channels, logging attendee vehicle license plates, and tracking nonviolent protest planning.

Surveillance extended to 18 major labor unions and grassroots organizations, including the AFL-CIO, SEIU, CWA, and the Sunrise Movement, with federal authorities obtaining years of financial and banking transaction records.

The intelligence operations were revealed in court filings by defense attorney Kevin Riach, who accused the government of conducting a politically driven, anti-democratic investigation to intimidate constitutionally protected dissent.
title: Documents show federal surveillance operation in Minnesota targeted progressive groups, unions

During a February 27 hearing, Magistrate Jessica Bartolozzi admonished Miller to attend all proceedings, while the congressman complained his schedule was unfair due to the GOP's "very small majority" before his attorney, Larry Zukerman, interrupted.

House Majority PAC plans to increase campaign advertising in Cleveland by roughly $6 million on Friday in response to Miller's decision to remain in his reelection race, raising total spending to roughly $7 million.

Under Ohio Professional Rules of Conduct Rule 3.3, attorneys must disclose if they realize material evidence presented is inaccurate, a standard Moreno's motion contends the congressman's legal team failed to meet.

summary: On Thursday, The Assembly Appropriations Committee spiked Senate Bill 1305, a proposal that would have required the California Department of Fish and Wildlife to evaluate reintroducing grizzly bears to the state.

Lawmakers rejected the study despite the grizzly's historical significance as California's state symbol, which dates to the 1846 Bear Flag Republic, even though the species was eradicated by the 1920s.

Proponents, including Native Americans, argued reintroduction would restore ecological balance; opponents such as ranchers and rural communities contended the state is too populated for an apex predator.
Democratic Assemblymember Buffy Wicks announced the decision without public discussion or testimony, as is typical for the committee, effectively halting the measure that lacked dedicated funding.

Reintroducing grizzlies to 21st-century California involves massive challenges, including land use pressures and genetic connectivity needs, as the state is no longer the wilderness of the 19th century.
title: California Lawmakers Kill Grizzly Bear Reintroduction Bill

summary: On Thursday, four beluga whales —Caspian, Peekachu, Rain, and Secord—arrived at Chicago's Shedd Aquarium from the closed Marineland of Canada, marking the second wave of an international rescue effort.

Marineland closed in 2024, prompting an urgent effort to rehome 30 belugas and four dolphins. After threatening euthanasia, the park reached an Ottawa-approved agreement to relocate animals to facilities in the United States and Spain.

Experts conducted an "intricate rescue," transporting the whales via custom-built slings, trucks, and planes. The animals are now under 24/7 observation within the Shedd's 3-million-gallon Abbott Oceanarium to monitor their health.

Veterinary teams observe the whales hour by hour, keeping new arrivals out of guests' view while they acclimate. Monitoring individual and social behaviors ensures successful integration into their new environment and pod.
The Shedd remains committed to housing two more belugas to reach its total of 10. International efforts continue as facilities relocate the remaining animals from the former Niagara Falls attraction.
title: Four More Belugas Arrive at Chicago Aquarium From Shuttered Canadian Theme Park

summary: On Thursday, District Judge Lynn Winmill blocked Idaho officials from enforcing the state's criminal abortion ban in cases where pregnancy threatens a patient's health or poses a risk of self-harm.
Since The Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, Idaho and a dozen other states have banned virtually all abortions, prompting a series of pending legal challenges nationwide.

Winmill's 81-page decision determined that the Fourteenth Amendment establishes a "narrow but fundamental right" to abortion when pregnancy threatens a woman's life or health, including severe mental health conditions.
Idaho Attorney General Raul Labrador intends to appeal the decision, while The Idaho Family Policy Center warned that civil liability for physicians remains under the state's 'Defense of Life' law.
A voter-led Initiative appearing on November ballots this year could overturn the ban entirely, potentially enumerating protections for women's reproductive healthcare and privacy into state law.
title: A federal judge blocks Idaho from prosecuting doctors for health-protecting abortions
